headline: 3 detained as phone recovered from suspect's house in 13-year-old's death
summary: Police recovered the iPhone belonging to the mother of Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, who was found dead near Comilla University.
details: 13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.
Police have recovered the iPhone belonging to the victim's mother from the house of a suspect named Tuhin.
Three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.
Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of Bangla at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.
The boy had left home on Friday afternoon, telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.
His body was recovered from the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of Cumilla nearly 24 hours after he went missing.
Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects to uncover the full details of the crime.
caption:
A 13-year-old boy's body was found near Comilla University; police have now recovered his mother's stolen iPhone from a suspect's home.

13-year-old Ishiat Shahriar Opratim, a Class VII student at Comilla Border Guard Public School, was found dead near Comilla University on Saturday afternoon.

Police have recovered the iPhone belonging to the victim's mother from the house of a suspect named Tuhin.

Three young men, identified as Tuhin, Anas, and Fahim, aged between 18 and 20, have been detained in connection with the alleged killing.

Opratim was the only son of Nahida Begum, an associate professor of Bangla at Comilla University, and businessman KM Firoz Shahriar.

The boy had left home on Friday afternoon, telling his parents he was going out to take photographs with his mother's iPhone.

His body was recovered from the Sananda hillocks on the outskirts of Cumilla nearly 24 hours after he went missing.

Police are currently analyzing CCTV footage and questioning the suspects to uncover the full details of the crime.

#Comilla #JusticeForOpratim #Bangladesh #CrimeNews #CumillaUniversity

Source: Prothom Alo, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune, Jamuna TV

headline: Three buses set on fire across Dhaka
summary: Two buses in Mirpur and one in Badda were engulfed in flames, causing chaos on the city's roads.
details: Three buses were set on fire in different parts of Dhaka, including Mirpur and Badda, causing significant disruption to traffic and panic among commuters.
In Mirpur, two moving buses were engulfed in flames, while another bus was set on fire in the Badda area.
Firefighters worked to bring the flames under control, as witnesses described scenes of chaos as passengers scrambled to escape the burning vehicles.
Authorities are investigating the cause of the fires to determine if they were accidental or intentional acts of arson.
